question: The EPLD update of the supervisor module has been scheduled for several Cisco MDS 9000 Series switches. What will be the impact of the update?
options: All traffic is stopped for the duration of the EPLD update and the switch is rebooted after the upgrade is completed.
The redundant supervisor takes over while the EPLD update is in progress and the switch is rebooted after the upgrade is completed.
All control plane traffic is stopped for the duration of the EPLD update and the switch remains operational for the duration of the upgrade.
The redundant supervisor takes over while the EPLD update is in progress and there is no service disruption.
theory: Updating the EPLDs on a supervisor module requires that supervisor to reload for the new hardware logic to take effect, and because the control plane lives on the supervisor, all traffic is stopped for the duration of that EPLD update and the switch reboots once it completes - the redundant supervisor cannot simply take over mid-update the way it can during a normal ISSU software upgrade, because the EPLD update itself must run on and reload the target supervisor. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 11 - EPLD Upgrade)
